class.name: InventoryItemInstance
class.brief_description: One item somebody has: a definition plus the state this copy carries.
class.description: Created by an [InventoryManagerComponent] on the server. Each instance has an [method get_item_id] that is unique across every inventory and the same on the server and its clients, so both sides can name the item to each other; it stays the same when the instance moves to another inventory. The state is stat tags - named counters such as ammo, charges or durability - and free-form data. Both replicate with the inventory. On a client the instance is a read-only mirror: its setters refuse there.

method.name: add_stat_tag_stack
method.description: Adds [param count] to the stat tag. A count below one does nothing.

method.name: find_fragment_by_class
method.description: Shortcut for [method InventoryItemDefinition.find_fragment_by_class] on this item's definition.

method.name: get_all_data
method.description: A copy of every per-instance value.

method.name: get_inventory
method.description: The inventory holding this instance right now, or [code]null[/code].

method.name: get_item_id
method.description: The id naming this instance on every peer.

method.name: get_stat_tags
method.description: A copy of every stat tag and its count.

method.name: has_stat_tag
method.description: Whether the stat tag's count is above zero.

method.name: remove_stat_tag_stack
method.description: Removes [param count] from the stat tag, never below zero. A count below one does nothing.

method.name: set_data
method.description: Stores a per-instance value (a colour, a name, contents). It must be something an RPC can carry - no objects. [code]null[/code] removes the key.

method.name: set_stat_tag_stack
method.description: Sets the stat tag to [param count]; zero removes it.

signal.name: data_changed
signal.description: A per-instance value changed or was removed ([param value] is [code]null[/code]).

signal.name: stat_tag_changed
signal.description: A stat tag's count changed - on the server and, when the change arrives, on clients holding a mirror.
